name: Motion (motion.dev)
description: The default animation engine for React (exit animations, layout/shared-element animation, gestures, springs) that also ships a small vanilla-JS API (animate, scroll, inView, stagger); pick it for component-level UI motion.
setup_notes: React: import { motion, AnimatePresence, MotionConfig } from "motion/react". Vanilla: import { animate, scroll, inView, stagger } from "motion". Formerly framer-motion; Motion One was merged into it. Use MotionConfig reducedMotion="user".

name: Motion for Vue (motion-v)
description: Vue port of Motion with the same declarative model (motion components, AnimatePresence, layout animations); pick it for Vue/Nuxt UI motion beyond <Transition>.
setup_notes: Import from "motion-v". Nuxt: add "motion-v/nuxt" to modules (auto-imports components; <motion /> still imported manually).

name: GSAP (GreenSock)
description: Framework-agnostic timeline engine for complex sequencing and scroll storytelling; all plugins (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, MorphSVG, ScrollSmoother, Flip) are free in the one package.
setup_notes: import { gsap } from "gsap"; import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger"; gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger). React: useGSAP from "@gsap/react" for automatic cleanup. Use gsap.matchMedia() for reduced-motion variants. @gsap/react only needed in React.

name: Lenis
description: Lightweight smooth-scroll that eases wheel input while keeping native document scrolling; pick it only for scroll-storytelling pages, not apps or docs.
setup_notes: import Lenis from "lenis" and "lenis/dist/lenis.css". React: import { ReactLenis, useLenis } from "lenis/react". With GSAP: lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update) and drive lenis.raf from gsap.ticker. Nested scrollers need data-lenis-prevent. No CSS scroll-snap without lenis/snap.

name: AutoAnimate (FormKit)
description: Zero-config animation of children being added, removed or moved in a parent; pick it for lists, todo items and filters when you want motion with one line.
setup_notes: Vanilla: autoAnimate(parentEl). React: useAutoAnimate from "@formkit/auto-animate/react". Vue: v-auto-animate or useAutoAnimate from "@formkit/auto-animate/vue". Disables itself under prefers-reduced-motion.

name: Anime.js v4
description: Lightweight framework-agnostic engine with timelines, stagger, SVG morph/draw, draggable, onScroll and splitText; pick it as a smaller GSAP alternative for vanilla projects.
setup_notes: v4 uses named ESM imports: import { animate, stagger, createTimeline } from "animejs". (v3 used a default anime() export; v4 code is not drop-in compatible.) Handle prefers-reduced-motion yourself.

name: react-spring
description: Spring-physics hooks for React (useSpring, useTransition, useTrail); pick it when physically based, interruptible values matter more than timelines.
setup_notes: import { useSpring, animated } from "@react-spring/web". Animate transform/opacity through animated components. Check React-version compatibility in the release notes before installing on React 19.

name: dotLottie web player (LottieFiles)
description: Official WASM player for .lottie and Lottie JSON animations exported from After Effects/Lottie Creator; pick it for designer-made vector motion graphics.
setup_notes: import { DotLottie } from "@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web" and render into a <canvas>. React: npm install @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react. Prefer over legacy lottie-web for new work. Pause or show a still frame under reduced motion; give the canvas an accessible label or aria-hidden.

name: Rive web runtime
description: Runtime for interactive Rive files with state machines driven by input or data; pick it for interactive illustrations, mascots and animated product UI made in the Rive editor.
setup_notes: Also @rive-app/canvas (smaller, Canvas2D) and @rive-app/react-canvas / @rive-app/react-webgl2. Call resizeDrawingSurfaceToCanvas() on load and cleanup() on unmount. Runtimes are open source; files are authored in the Rive editor.

name: three.js
description: The standard WebGL/WebGPU 3D library; listed here ONLY for 3D scenes (hero objects, product viewers, shader backgrounds), not for UI motion.
setup_notes: import * as THREE from "three". Heavy: lazy-load below the fold or after first paint; pause the render loop off-screen and under reduced motion; provide a static fallback image.

name: React Three Fiber
description: React renderer for three.js; listed ONLY for 3D scenes in React apps (pairs with @react-three/drei helpers), not for UI motion.
setup_notes: v9 pairs with React 19 (v8 with React 18). Next.js: add "three" to transpilePackages. Lazy-load the <Canvas>, set frameloop="demand" when static, and respect reduced motion.
